saints.name: St. Paschal Baylon
saints.title: Religious
saints.shortBlurb: A Spanish shepherd-boy turned Franciscan lay brother, burning with love for the Blessed Sacrament…
biography: Born to peasant parents in Aragon in 1540, Paschal tended sheep in his youth and taught himself to read from a borrowed book so that he might follow the Mass. At about twenty-four he entered the Franciscans as a lay brother, serving as porter, cook, and doorkeeper with unfailing humility.

His whole life was marked by an intense devotion to the Eucharist, before which he would kneel for hours. He died at Villareal in 1592, reputedly at the moment of the elevation at Mass, and was canonized in 1690; Pope Leo XIII later named him patron of Eucharistic congresses and confraternities.
saints.knownFor: His ardent devotion to the Blessed Sacrament.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 17 May
